subject: Cost/pricing follow-up — token volumes & latency tradeoffs (post-call)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya@fintechai.com>, Jacob Lee <jacob.lee@fintechai.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-10T15:05:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up & numbers from today's discovery call — cost + latency trade-offs

Thanks again for your time today — great discussion. Quick recap and next steps so we keep momentum:

1) Usage profile (what we heard):
- Primary flow: contextual chat for end users (short prompts, 150-400 tokens per response on average)
- Expected steady-state: ~8M tokens/day (peak 2x), monthly ~240M tokens
- Burst pattern: morning block + daily batch jobs for summaries (infrequent large contexts)

2) SLOs and constraints you shared:
- P95 latency target for chat: ~200ms end-to-end
- Budget: looking for target unit economics in the $/1M tokens range (you mentioned $20–$40 as a reference)
- Data controls: sensitive PII, so Private/Dedicated considerations may apply for production

3) Quick recommendations (high level):
- If strict p95 200ms: prefer Dedicated (reserved) capacity or high-tier Hosted with streaming enabled.
- If absolute unit-cost is most important and you can relax p95 (or accept batching for non-critical flows): Dedicated or Private with quantized weights + larger batching gives best $/1M.
- Streaming is great for perceived latency on chat while still enabling batching for background jobs.

4) Next steps I promised:
- Share our pricing deck and an initial mutual action plan (attached).
- Confirm an exact target $/1M token goal and a 2-week PoC scope (1M tokens test for perf/cost).
- Align on whether you want Hosted higher-tier vs Dedicated trial.

Attaching: Redwood_pricing_deck.pdf (pricing tiers, sample unit economics, example configs)

Would you confirm the daily token range (low/expected/high) and the budget target you want us to optimize for? Happy to propose two concrete configs (1) low-latency: streaming + small batch, expected $/1M and (2) low-cost: larger batch + quantization, expected $/1M.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Date: 2026-07-11T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up & numbers from today's discovery call — cost + latency trade-offs

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful. A few clarifications from our side:

- Token volumes: our initial conservative rollout is closer to 4–6M tokens/day (monthly ~120–180M), but with growth to 15–20M tokens/day in 6–9 months if adoption ramps.
- Budget target: finance is pushing for a target of ~$15–$25 per 1M tokens as a long-term goal. For the PoC phase we can accept a higher $/1M to prove latency and quality.
- Latency: for the customer-facing chat flow we really want p95 under 250ms. For background summary jobs latency is fine to be several seconds.
- Security: we'll need SOC 2 evidence and a brief on where logs and KV cache are stored for private data.

Can you also confirm:
1) Rough $/1M for Hosted standard streaming config vs Dedicated reserved (with a 12-month commit)
2) Typical batching windows you recommend (ms) and how they affect p95

Happy to book a follow-up next week to review configs.

--
Priya Shah
Head of Product, AI | FinTechAI
priya@fintechai.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya@fintechai.com>, Jacob Lee <jacob.lee@fintechai.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-12T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up & numbers from today's discovery call — cost + latency trade-offs

Thanks Priya — great constraints. Short answers up front, then a proposed config table and next steps.

1) Rough $/1M (estimates, will refine in pricing deck):
- Hosted (standard, streaming-enabled): ~$22–$30 per 1M tokens depending on model and concurrency
- Dedicated (reserved 12mo commit, optimized quantized models): ~$9–$16 per 1M tokens depending on commit size and model variant
- Private on-prem (customer-managed infra, with Redwood runtime): ~$6–$12 per 1M tokens (operational cost transfer + infra)

2) Batching windows and p95 trade-offs:
- Aggressive micro-batching (10–30ms window): can reduce per-token cost notably for high QPS flows while keeping additional latency <30ms on average; still keeps p95 reasonable but depends on queueing during bursts.
- Larger batching (50–200ms): best cost savings but will add to tail latency — risky for strict p95 <250ms user-facing flows.
- Streaming + immediate partial token flush: we can combine streaming with behind-the-scenes continuous batching for non-blocking generation to balance perceived latency and cost.

Proposed starter configs for PoC (based on 4–6M steady tokens/day):
A) Low-latency PoC (goal p95 <250ms): Hosted high-tier + streaming, small batch window (10–30ms), expected cost ~$25–$30 /1M tokens for PoC
B) Cost-optimized PoC (goal $/1M <= $18): Dedicated reserved (small pool) + quantized model + batch window ~40–80ms, expected cost ~$12–$16 /1M tokens

Notes: exact numbers depend on model choice (Llama3-large vs opt- variants), quantization level (4-bit/8-bit), and expected concurrency. We'll run a 1M-token PoC to measure real p95 and unit cost and then pick path to production.

Attachments: I attached a proposed mutual action plan (PoC milestones, success metrics, owners).

Next steps:
- Can you confirm PoC scope (we propose 1M tokens test over 48–72 hours with both configs A and B)?
- I'll loop in our solutions engineer (Dev) to scope the test and schedule a 60-min sync to provision Dedicated trial if you prefer that path.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales Lead | Redwood Inference
